summary: Pulaski County, Missouri, lookout of the Missouri Conservation Commission; its 17.6-acre towersite was acquired in fiscal 1948-49. Sources do not describe its fate.

events.note: 17.6-acre towersite acquired in fiscal 1948-49, per the Missouri Conservation Commission annual report as quoted on the Central US Lookouts page

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence: one Central US Lookouts entry (agency, county, land description and the 1948-49 towersite acquisition) plus the MDC general history of fire towers, which says nothing about Swede in particular. No build date, height, design, staffing, access or fate was found in any source read. UNRESOLVED RELOCATION CLAIM: a Missouri Conservation history post on Facebook (https://www.facebook.com/MCC1010/photos/swede-fire-lookout-tower-and-entry-sign-the-swede-tower-was-originally-located-i/1042869921210777/), seen only as a search snippet, says the Swede tower was relocated to Proctor, Missouri, in 1974. The Central US Lookouts Proctor page (https://centraluslookouts.weebly.com/proctor.html) instead says a steel tower moved from the Gasconade district replaced the original wooden tower at Proctor in 1974, and does not mention Swede. The Facebook post could not be opened (fetch returned only its title), so the story leaves out any move. Open that post before writing any fate or today section. The brief's coordinates (37.91921, -92.36823) were not checked against a source describing the tower site.
